$comment: `usage`: the words after the verb's own, where its `what` does not begin with them. What a newcomer reads in a command's `--help` for the cli's own commands, by their words (contracts/shapes VerbHelp; core/help renders it). A package's commands carry the same `help` in their manifest rows.

setup.when: once per repository, after you install atlasbound; at its top or in any folder inside it
setup.changes: .claude/settings.local.json, .claude/commands/, a block in .gitignore, and the team notice row in .claude/settings.json in a clone nobody set up yet; nothing outside this repository; a file of yours at one of its command paths stops it before it writes anything, naming that file

flags.--only <a,b>: connect only these modules (atlasbound modules names them)
flags.--without <a>: connect every module but this one
flags.--with <a>: also connect a module that stays off unless you name it
flags.--team-notice: write or refresh only the team notice row in .claude/settings.json, then commit it

update.when: after you installed a newer version with npm
update.changes: the same files as setup, rewritten for this version

modules.when: before you turn a module on or off

modules on.when: to use a module here that is off: only you turn one on, an AI session asks you to
modules on.changes: adds its hooks and slash commands to .claude/ and its lines to the .gitignore block

modules off.when: when you do not want a module in this repository
modules off.changes: takes its hooks, slash commands and allow rules out of .claude/; its plans and notes stay

uninstall.when: when you stop using AtlasBound in this repository
uninstall.changes: takes out what setup wrote; your plans in .decisionbook/ stay unless you add --purge

flags.--purge: also delete the data kept here and in your home for this repository; it names each before you type the phrase

doctor.when: right after setup, after an upgrade, and whenever something seems off
doctor.changes: nothing in your files; it asks the hooks one test question and keeps a trace record
doctor.exit: 0 when it ends "doctor: ok"; 1 when it found a problem, each named with what to do

status.when: for a quick look; doctor checks more

leftovers.when: once after an upgrade from 0.23 or 0.24, or when doctor names leftovers

leftovers remove.when: after atlasbound leftovers listed something, and every AI session opened before the upgrade is closed
leftovers remove.changes: your AI host's user settings and its own file lose the old rows and server; the old files leave ~/.atlasbound; a copy of each is kept; nothing while the earlier version's server still runs

hook.when: never by hand: the hooks setup wrote run it, with the host's event as JSON on standard input
hook.changes: the trace in .atlasbound/; a check may hold a write or the end of a turn

help.when: whenever you wonder what a command does

flags.--all: every command with its line, in three groups

version.when: to see which version is installed

debug trace.line: show what the product recorded: the steps of a run and how each ended
debug trace.when: when something went wrong and you want to see why

flags.--last: the newest run that did work
flags.--session <id>: the runs of one AI session

debug doctor.line: doctor's whole answer as JSON, for a script or your AI
debug doctor.when: when a tool, not a person, reads the check

debug shell.line: show which files a shell command would write, as the checks read it
debug shell.when: when a check held a command and you want to see why

debug who.line: say whether a command counts as yours or as the AI session's, and why
debug who.when: when a command was refused as "you only"

debug inject.line: replay a session's hook events from a file on a scratch copy and count what each part told the AI
debug inject.when: to measure how much the product adds to an AI session
debug inject.changes: nothing here; a scratch copy, deleted after
